facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: IRON MOUNTAIN INC is a growing, highly levered REIT whose reported leverage on its own Adjusted EBITDA is around six times and whose free cash flow after capital expenditure is negative. For the twelve months to September 30, 2026 (LTM Q3 2026), Adjusted EBITDA is 2,888,192 thousand (FY2025 2,573,950 plus nine months 2026 2,182,915 less nine months 2025 1,868,673), revenue is 7,799.0 US$m and the Adjusted EBITDA margin is 37.0%. Total debt at carrying amount is 17,972.2 US$m, so total debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 6.22x and net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 6.16x, against 6.38x and 6.32x at FY2025. Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest paid is 3.16x on an LTM basis against 3.12x at FY2025. These ratios improved against FY2025 because Adjusted EBITDA grew faster than debt, but total debt over Adjusted EBITDA edged up from 6.19x at LTM Q2 2026 to 6.22x at LTM Q3 2026.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: IRON MOUNTAIN INC is a listed US real estate investment trust with no sponsor or controlling owner disclosed in the pinned sources. Its credit rests on three operating blocks that behave differently. Global RIM (records management, data management, digital solutions, shredding, media and consumer storage) is the recurring core: FY2025 segment revenue was 5,291,481 thousand and segment Adjusted EBITDA 2,363,498 thousand. Management says a majority of revenue is recurring, storage contracts run one to five years and no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue; all three are management or filing statements and the sources give no volume data beyond stating that volume is expected to be relatively stable, so growth in this segment comes from revenue management (pricing). Global Data Center is the growth engine: FY2025 revenue 803,429 thousand, Adjusted EBITDA 416,326 thousand, with nine-month 2026 revenue up 39.6% on lease commencements. It also absorbs most of the capital: nine-month 2026 data center growth capex was 1,344,097 thousand of 1,589,574 thousand total growth capex. Corporate and Other (ALM, Fine Arts and corporate costs) grew revenue 55.9% in nine months 2026 partly through acquisitions and reports negative segment Adjusted EBITDA (109,611 thousand loss) because corporate costs sit in it.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: For a creditor the transmission mechanism is: recurring storage cash flow plus long data center leases (weighted average lease expiration 10.3 years at December 31, 2025) give revenue visibility; the same data center growth consumes cash ahead of revenue, so debt rose to 17,972,202 thousand while operating cash flow of 1,203,634 thousand trailed capex of 1,724,205 thousand (CP-1). The 2026 transactions were financings, not a change of control: a 1,500,000 thousand note issue, two data center project financings, a receivables program upsize and one new joint venture with an unnamed partner. The credit implication is refinancing and market-access dependence rather than sponsor or ownership risk, and the sources do not allow an ownership or sponsor-behaviour assessment beyond documented issuer actions. Governance of creditor-relevant behaviour is Neutral or Mixed: distributions are tied to REIT status and are rising while free cash flow is negative, but there is no documented priming, uptiering, drop-down or collateral release.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: In Q2 2026, on June 26, 2026, IMI completed a private offering of 1,500,000 thousand of 6 1/4% Notes due 2035, issued at par with a maturity of January 15, 2035, interest paid January 15 and July 15 and a par call date of July 15, 2031; net proceeds of about 1,481,800 thousand repaid part of the revolving credit facility borrowings and funded general corporate purposes (10-Q Q3 page:22-23). The Q2 2026 quarterly report prints the par call date as July 15, 2031 in its debt note (10-Q Q2 page:21) and as July 15, 2029 in its MD&A table (10-Q Q2 page:47); both spans are quoted in the conflicts table and the conflict is logged, not reconciled. In Q1 2026, on January 9, 2026, two wholly-owned subsidiaries entered into mortgage and mezzanine loans with a total original principal of 433,000 thousand (Virginia 3 Term Loans due 2031, maturing January 9, 2031, weighted average rate 6.3%), used to repay the earlier Virginia 3 loans and part of the revolver (10-Q Q3 page:21). On June 9, 2026, Iron Mountain Data Centers Virginia 9, LLC entered into a credit agreement allowing term loans up to 298,000 thousand at SOFR plus 3.00%, maturing June 9, 2029 with two one-year extension options, with 138,627 thousand outstanding at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:21-22). In the same quarter the company formed Iron Mountain Data Centers Virginia 9 JV, LP with an unnamed partner, creating initial noncontrolling interests of about 49,900 thousand (10-Q Q3 page:24). On May 28, 2026 the receivables securitization program was amended to include certain Canadian entities, increase capacity from 400,000 thousand to 450,000 thousand and extend maturity from July 1, 2027 to July 1, 2029 (10-Q Q3 page:22).

facts.text: Other items in the period: a finance lease expected to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026 with a 31-year term and about 223,400 thousand of undiscounted minimum payments (10-Q Q3 page:10); acquisitions in the ALM business, with cash paid for acquisitions of 8,033 thousand in nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:6) and a 31.7 million increase in Corporate and Other service revenue attributed to acquisitions (10-Q Q3 page:44); and the deferred purchase obligation for the 2024 Regency Technologies acquisition, which has an earnout of up to 200,000 thousand payable in 2027 if earned and a fair value of 210,188 thousand at September 30, 2026 (10-K page:134; 10-Q Q3 page:10-11). The creditor effect is that the 2026 issuance extended the bond stack to 2035 and moved some bank borrowing into fixed rate notes, while project debt at subsidiaries and a new joint venture add structurally senior and noncontrolling claims; the stated use of proceeds was repayment of existing revolver borrowings, which in my reading restored revolver capacity rather than adding committed liquidity (Analyst Interpretation). Subsequent events up to the cutoff: the board declared a dividend of 0.993 per share on November 5, 2026, payable January 6, 2027 to holders of record on December 15, 2026, and management raised full-year 2026 guidance; both are subsequent to the September 30, 2026 balance sheet and are not folded into period facts (10-Q Q3 page:24; Release Q3 page:2). No new debt issue after September 30, 2026 appears in the sources.

rows.label: Iron Mountain is a public REIT with a recurring storage base and a fast-growing data center segment, funded largely by debt. Its 2026 financing was bond, project loan and joint-venture based, with no sponsor.
Global RIM generated revenue of 5,291,481 thousand and Adjusted EBITDA of 2,363,498 thousand in FY2025, with no customer above about 3% of revenue.
Data center revenue grew 39.6% in nine months 2026 to 791,194 thousand, and management reports leasing of 137 megawatts year to date.
New 2026 debt was a 1,500,000 thousand 6 1/4% note due 2035, 433,000 thousand Virginia 3 loans due 2031 and a 298,000 thousand Virginia 9 facility.
Dividends are rising: 0.993 per share was declared on November 5, 2026, up 15%, while operating cash flow after capex is negative.
The indentures treat leveraged recapitalizations as not a change of control.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: IRON MOUNTAIN INC is a large, diversified and cash-generative REIT whose debt load, at 6.22x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, is high and still growing, so the credit view is cautious: sound operations on a stretched balance sheet. The strongest support is a recurring storage business with Global RIM revenue of USD 5,291.5 million and no customer above about 3%, plus a data center segment growing 39.6% with a 53.6% margin. The weakest point is that nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 1,203.6 million fell short of capex of USD 1,724.2 million and dividends of USD 790.0 million. The outcome is decided by whether data center leases commence on schedule and whether the company keeps refinancing, including USD 1,000.0 million of notes due September 15, 2027, at acceptable cost. [Confidence: Medium; Analyst Interpretation.]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: IRON MOUNTAIN INC carries total debt of USD 17,972.2 million at September 30, 2026, which is 6.22x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,888.2 million and 6.16x on a net basis, compared with 6.38x and 6.32x at FY2025. Leverage fell against FY2025 because Adjusted EBITDA grew faster than debt, but it rose slightly from 6.19x at LTM Q2 2026, and a stricter measure that does not add back stock-based compensation, restructuring or acquisition costs (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) gives 6.81x. Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back items such as stock-based compensation, so the headline ratios understate leverage on a stricter basis.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. The recurring storage base is the first strength: Global RIM contributes most segment profit, management states a majority of revenue is recurring, storage contracts run one to five years and no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue, so cash flow is not exposed to a single name. The data center segment is a second strength, because long leases with a weighted average expiration of 10.3 years at December 31, 2025 and a segment margin that rose to 53.6% give visibility on a growing earnings layer. Third, reported covenant headroom is wide and the revolver, which matures in 2030, has USD 2,218.2 million available, which supports liquidity for the next twelve months despite near-term maturities. Fourth, funding is diversified across notes, bank debt, project loans and a receivables program, and the 2026 issuance extended the note stack to 2035. All are tagged Documentary Fact except the recurring-revenue share and the leasing pace, which are Management Language.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Leverage of 6.22x on a management EBITDA measure, and 6.81x on a stricter measure, leaves limited tolerance for an earnings shortfall. Free cash flow is negative before dividends and the company has raised its dividend while borrowing, so debt rises each year while the data center build runs; the REIT distribution rules and a stated commitment to dividend growth increase financing needs. Refinancing exposure is concentrated in 2027 to 2030. Project debt and a new joint venture add structurally senior and noncontrolling claims at subsidiaries that sit ahead of parent noteholders, and the parent notes depend on subsidiary guarantors and cash upstream. The ALM business relies on a limited number of clients and China-based buyers, and Corporate and Other carries negative segment Adjusted EBITDA after corporate costs. Ownership, contract backlog and ratings are not supplied, which limits the assessment of business risk; missing evidence is not treated as adverse.

Nothing in the set is draft, unsigned or blocked at preparation. The filed annual and quarterly reports control their respective facts; the releases carry attributed management claims and must not override the filings. This is a statement of source sufficiency only (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY); it does not evaluate any downstream input contract (CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED) and asserts no normalized quarter, reconciliation or downstream acceptance.

### Source relationships and conflicts

The three quarterly reports and the annual report are separate active sources for different dates; none replaces another. The balance sheet date of the Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 reports differ, and each carries the December 31, 2025 balance sheet as comparative, which can be checked against the annual report. The three releases duplicate content that also appears in the matching quarterly reports (revenue, net income, Adjusted EBITDA). The filing controls where they overlap; the Q3 2026 release (page:10) and the Q3 2026 quarterly report (page:42) show the same Adjusted EBITDA for the nine months, as quoted above, so no value conflict was found on that item.

Conflict 1, severity low. The Q2 2026 quarterly report prints the par call date of the 2035 notes as July 15, 2031 in its debt note (page:21) but as July 15, 2029 in its MD&A debt table (page:47). The Q3 2026 quarterly report prints July 15, 2031 in its note (page:22) and in its MD&A (page:49). The later filing and the Q2 note agree, so the 2029 entry is treated as an error in the Q2 MD&A table. Downstream effect: any call-date statement on those notes should cite the Q3 2026 report and not the Q2 MD&A table.

No other conflict between sources was found in the items searched: debt table totals, revolver availability, letters of credit and covenant ratios were each read in the Q3 2026 report and compared where an earlier report printed the same item.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Total debt is 17,972,202 thousand, 6.22x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 2,888,192 thousand. Operating cash flow trails capex and dividends, so debt keeps rising. | Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Total debt rose to 17,972,202 thousand at September 30, 2026 from 16,431,959 thousand at December 31, 2025, while LTM Adjusted EBITDA reached 2,888,192 thousand. | Leverage on Adjusted EBITDA eased to 6.22x from 6.38x, but absolute debt keeps growing. | High |

| Operating cash flow of 1,203,634 thousand for nine months 2026 was below capex of 1,724,205 thousand and dividends of 789,997 thousand. | The business relies on debt and joint-venture capital to fund growth and distributions. | High |

| Cash plus revolver availability was 2,406,378 thousand at September 30, 2026, down from 2,912,367 thousand at June 30, 2026. | Liquidity is ample, but the revolver drawing rose by 489,500 thousand in one quarter. | High |

| Credit Agreement ratios are 4.8x lease adjusted leverage (maximum 7.0x) and 2.5x fixed charge cover (minimum 1.5x). | Reported covenant headroom is wide, but it cannot be rebuilt from Adjusted EBITDA. | Medium |

| Current portion of debt rose to 1,232,903 thousand from 216,074 thousand, including notes due September 15, 2027. | A refinancing event falls inside twelve months of the balance sheet date. | Medium |
### Financial base view

IRON MOUNTAIN INC is a growing, highly levered REIT whose reported leverage on its own Adjusted EBITDA is around six times and whose free cash flow after capital expenditure is negative. For the twelve months to September 30, 2026 (LTM Q3 2026), Adjusted EBITDA is 2,888,192 thousand (FY2025 2,573,950 plus nine months 2026 2,182,915 less nine months 2025 1,868,673), revenue is 7,799.0 US$m and the Adjusted EBITDA margin is 37.0%. Total debt at carrying amount is 17,972.2 US$m, so total debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 6.22x and net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA is 6.16x, against 6.38x and 6.32x at FY2025. Adjusted EBITDA to cash interest paid is 3.16x on an LTM basis against 3.12x at FY2025. These ratios improved against FY2025 because Adjusted EBITDA grew faster than debt, but total debt over Adjusted EBITDA edged up from 6.19x at LTM Q2 2026 to 6.22x at LTM Q3 2026.

Cash generation does not cover the investment programme. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure is negative 520.6 US$m for nine months 2026 and negative 536.8 US$m LTM, before 790.0 US$m of nine-month dividends. Financing in the period included 1,500,000 thousand principal of new 6 1/4% notes due 2035 (net proceeds of 1,485,000 thousand in the cash flow statement), data center project loan and revolver borrowings, and 95.2 US$m of noncontrolling interest equity contributions; the filings do not tie each source to the funding gap. The Credit Agreement covenant ratios (4.8x and 2.5x) show wide reported headroom, but they are EBITDAR and EBITDA based with adjustments and the filings state they are not directly comparable to Adjusted EBITDA. Liquidity of 2,406.4 US$m is cash plus revolver availability only; other undrawn lines are small, project specific or tied to eligible receivables. The Adjusted EBITDA definition adds back stock-based compensation and other items, so a stricter operating income plus depreciation and amortization measure gives a higher LTM leverage of 6.81x (calculation below); both are shown and neither is a covenant measure.

## Findings
### Reader summary

### Business and transaction view

IRON MOUNTAIN INC is a listed US real estate investment trust with no sponsor or controlling owner disclosed in the pinned sources. Its credit rests on three operating blocks that behave differently. Global RIM (records management, data management, digital solutions, shredding, media and consumer storage) is the recurring core: FY2025 segment revenue was 5,291,481 thousand and segment Adjusted EBITDA 2,363,498 thousand. Management says a majority of revenue is recurring, storage contracts run one to five years and no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue; all three are management or filing statements and the sources give no volume data beyond stating that volume is expected to be relatively stable, so growth in this segment comes from revenue management (pricing). Global Data Center is the growth engine: FY2025 revenue 803,429 thousand, Adjusted EBITDA 416,326 thousand, with nine-month 2026 revenue up 39.6% on lease commencements. It also absorbs most of the capital: nine-month 2026 data center growth capex was 1,344,097 thousand of 1,589,574 thousand total growth capex. Corporate and Other (ALM, Fine Arts and corporate costs) grew revenue 55.9% in nine months 2026 partly through acquisitions and reports negative segment Adjusted EBITDA (109,611 thousand loss) because corporate costs sit in it.

For a creditor the transmission mechanism is: recurring storage cash flow plus long data center leases (weighted average lease expiration 10.3 years at December 31, 2025) give revenue visibility; the same data center growth consumes cash ahead of revenue, so debt rose to 17,972,202 thousand while operating cash flow of 1,203,634 thousand trailed capex of 1,724,205 thousand (CP-1). The 2026 transactions were financings, not a change of control: a 1,500,000 thousand note issue, two data center project financings, a receivables program upsize and one new joint venture with an unnamed partner. The credit implication is refinancing and market-access dependence rather than sponsor or ownership risk, and the sources do not allow an ownership or sponsor-behaviour assessment beyond documented issuer actions. Governance of creditor-relevant behaviour is Neutral or Mixed: distributions are tied to REIT status and are rising while free cash flow is negative, but there is no documented priming, uptiering, drop-down or collateral release.

There is no sponsor transaction, leveraged buyout or change of control in the sources, so the transaction view is the set of financing and investment events in the period. All items below are completed unless stated, and each is a Documentary Fact from the cited filing.

In Q2 2026, on June 26, 2026, IMI completed a private offering of 1,500,000 thousand of 6 1/4% Notes due 2035, issued at par with a maturity of January 15, 2035, interest paid January 15 and July 15 and a par call date of July 15, 2031; net proceeds of about 1,481,800 thousand repaid part of the revolving credit facility borrowings and funded general corporate purposes (10-Q Q3 page:22-23). The Q2 2026 quarterly report prints the par call date as July 15, 2031 in its debt note (10-Q Q2 page:21) and as July 15, 2029 in its MD&A table (10-Q Q2 page:47); both spans are quoted in the conflicts table and the conflict is logged, not reconciled. In Q1 2026, on January 9, 2026, two wholly-owned subsidiaries entered into mortgage and mezzanine loans with a total original principal of 433,000 thousand (Virginia 3 Term Loans due 2031, maturing January 9, 2031, weighted average rate 6.3%), used to repay the earlier Virginia 3 loans and part of the revolver (10-Q Q3 page:21). On June 9, 2026, Iron Mountain Data Centers Virginia 9, LLC entered into a credit agreement allowing term loans up to 298,000 thousand at SOFR plus 3.00%, maturing June 9, 2029 with two one-year extension options, with 138,627 thousand outstanding at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:21-22). In the same quarter the company formed Iron Mountain Data Centers Virginia 9 JV, LP with an unnamed partner, creating initial noncontrolling interests of about 49,900 thousand (10-Q Q3 page:24). On May 28, 2026 the receivables securitization program was amended to include certain Canadian entities, increase capacity from 400,000 thousand to 450,000 thousand and extend maturity from July 1, 2027 to July 1, 2029 (10-Q Q3 page:22).

Other items in the period: a finance lease expected to commence in the fourth quarter of 2026 with a 31-year term and about 223,400 thousand of undiscounted minimum payments (10-Q Q3 page:10); acquisitions in the ALM business, with cash paid for acquisitions of 8,033 thousand in nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:6) and a 31.7 million increase in Corporate and Other service revenue attributed to acquisitions (10-Q Q3 page:44); and the deferred purchase obligation for the 2024 Regency Technologies acquisition, which has an earnout of up to 200,000 thousand payable in 2027 if earned and a fair value of 210,188 thousand at September 30, 2026 (10-K page:134; 10-Q Q3 page:10-11). The creditor effect is that the 2026 issuance extended the bond stack to 2035 and moved some bank borrowing into fixed rate notes, while project debt at subsidiaries and a new joint venture add structurally senior and noncontrolling claims; the stated use of proceeds was repayment of existing revolver borrowings, which in my reading restored revolver capacity rather than adding committed liquidity (Analyst Interpretation). ### Credit view

IRON MOUNTAIN INC is a large, diversified and cash-generative REIT whose debt load, at 6.22x LTM Adjusted EBITDA, is high and still growing, so the credit view is cautious: sound operations on a stretched balance sheet. The strongest support is a recurring storage business with Global RIM revenue of USD 5,291.5 million and no customer above about 3%, plus a data center segment growing 39.6% with a 53.6% margin. The weakest point is that nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 1,203.6 million fell short of capex of USD 1,724.2 million and dividends of USD 790.0 million. The outcome is decided by whether data center leases commence on schedule and whether the company keeps refinancing, including USD 1,000.0 million of notes due September 15, 2027, at acceptable cost. [Confidence: Medium; Analyst Interpretation.]
### Key findings

IRON MOUNTAIN INC carries total debt of USD 17,972.2 million at September 30, 2026, which is 6.22x LTM Adjusted EBITDA of USD 2,888.2 million and 6.16x on a net basis, compared with 6.38x and 6.32x at FY2025. Leverage fell against FY2025 because Adjusted EBITDA grew faster than debt, but it rose slightly from 6.19x at LTM Q2 2026, and a stricter measure that does not add back stock-based compensation, restructuring or acquisition costs (operating income plus depreciation and amortization) gives 6.81x. Adjusted EBITDA is a management measure that adds back items such as stock-based compensation, so the headline ratios understate leverage on a stricter basis.

The company does not fund its investment programme from operations. Nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of USD 1,203.6 million was below capex of USD 1,724.2 million, a shortfall of USD 520.6 million before USD 790.0 million of dividends. Debt rose from USD 16,432.0 million at December 31, 2025, and the cash flow statement shows senior note proceeds and noncontrolling interest contributions as sources. Data center growth capex dominates the spending, so the credit improves only as leased capacity commences and converts to revenue.

Liquidity is ample but moving down. Cash of USD 188.2 million and revolver availability of USD 2,218.2 million give USD 2,406.4 million, against USD 2,912.4 million at June 30, 2026, because revolver borrowings rose by USD 489.5 million in Q3 2026. Interest cover is steady: Adjusted EBITDA is 3.16x cash interest paid on an LTM basis against 3.12x at FY2025, and the weighted average interest rate is 5.7%.

Near-term refinancing is the main event risk. The current portion of long-term debt is USD 1,232.9 million, which includes the USD 1,000.0 million 4 7/8% notes due September 15, 2027. The last company-printed maturity table (December 31, 2025) shows USD 2,330.8 million due in 2027, USD 1,663.7 million in 2028, USD 2,137.5 million in 2029 and USD 3,035.7 million in 2030; some of that has since been extended or refinanced, but no later table is printed. The Credit Agreement tests show 4.8x lease adjusted leverage against a 7.0x maximum and 2.5x fixed charge coverage against a 1.5x minimum, so reported headroom is wide, although those ratios use other definitions than Adjusted EBITDA and cannot be rebuilt from the sources.

On the business side, Global RIM generated USD 5,291.5 million of revenue and USD 2,363.5 million of segment Adjusted EBITDA in FY2025, and nine-month 2026 data center revenue was USD 791.2 million, up 39.6%. Management reports leasing of 137 megawatts year to date, which is signed capacity, not commenced revenue. The board raised the quarterly dividend by 15% to USD 0.993 per share on November 5, 2026, and the indentures do not treat a leveraged recapitalization as a change of control, so event protection for noteholders is limited. No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed, which removes sponsor extraction as a driver but also leaves ownership unassessed.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. The recurring storage base is the first strength: Global RIM contributes most segment profit, management states a majority of revenue is recurring, storage contracts run one to five years and no customer exceeds about 3% of revenue, so cash flow is not exposed to a single name. The data center segment is a second strength, because long leases with a weighted average expiration of 10.3 years at December 31, 2025 and a segment margin that rose to 53.6% give visibility on a growing earnings layer. Third, reported covenant headroom is wide and the revolver, which matures in 2030, has USD 2,218.2 million available, which supports liquidity for the next twelve months despite near-term maturities. Fourth, funding is diversified across notes, bank debt, project loans and a receivables program, and the 2026 issuance extended the note stack to 2035. All are tagged Documentary Fact except the recurring-revenue share and the leasing pace, which are Management Language.

Weaknesses. Leverage of 6.22x on a management EBITDA measure, and 6.81x on a stricter measure, leaves limited tolerance for an earnings shortfall. Free cash flow is negative before dividends and the company has raised its dividend while borrowing, so debt rises each year while the data center build runs; the REIT distribution rules and a stated commitment to dividend growth increase financing needs. Refinancing exposure is concentrated in 2027 to 2030. Project debt and a new joint venture add structurally senior and noncontrolling claims at subsidiaries that sit ahead of parent noteholders, and the parent notes depend on subsidiary guarantors and cash upstream. The ALM business relies on a limited number of clients and China-based buyers, and Corporate and Other carries negative segment Adjusted EBITDA after corporate costs. Ownership, contract backlog and ratings are not supplied, which limits the assessment of business risk; missing evidence is not treated as adverse.

Readiness: CP-2 is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. CP-0 judged the source set ready with limitations, CP-1 and CP-1A were accepted, and CP-1A judged CP-2 as ready with limitations, so confidence is held below High.
